summary: Re-verified the page-by-page trust explanation feature after the banned-jargon fix from iteration_18. All 7 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_page_explanations.py now PASS (previously 6/7). The critical test test_get_page_explanations_schema_and_personalization now passes — 0 banned words across all 6 explanation pages for the seeded Michael Thompson case. Manual curl verification also confirms: status=completed, pages_total=6, explanations=6, banned hits=[], and every page mentions Michael/Sarah/James. Regenerate endpoint returns 200 with task_id. Regression on /trust-draft-explanation and /extract-status still passes. Server alive.
critical_code_review_comments: trust_page_explainer._scrub_jargon is a clean, minimal post-generation safety net — regex list is comprehensive and covers both quoted and unquoted forms. Good defense-in-depth alongside the strengthened SYSTEM_PROMPT.
Consider adding a metric/log line when _scrub_jargon actually mutates output, so drift in the LLM's compliance can be observed over time.

test_regenerate_no_draft_returns_400 needed timeout bumped from 30s to 90s for /api/admin/trust-cases listing — the endpoint appears slow for large case lists; may warrant pagination or an admin index.
seed_data_creation: None. Used pre-seeded Michael Thompson case 8eb42bd3-5d43-43f2-b765-b98a144bd931.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Banned-jargon issue from iteration_18 is fully resolved. Both the strengthened SYSTEM_PROMPT and the _scrub_jargon() regex post-processor work as designed. 7/7 tests pass. If re-running: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_page_explanations.py -v — takes ~50s if the seeded case already has completed explanations, longer if regenerated first.
rca_of_the_issue: Fix from iteration_18 has been verified. Root cause was the LLM quoting banned Latin terms while trying to define them in plain English. Fix layered two defenses: (1) SYSTEM_PROMPT and user_prompt both now explicitly forbid even QUOTING the banned words and provide approved plain-English substitutes; (2) _scrub_jargon() runs a regex sweep on every LLM output before persistence, replacing any leaked term (quoted or unquoted) with a plain-English alias. Verified 0 leaks across 6 pages of freshly generated explanations.
